Bachelor's degree in related area and / or equivalent experience / training
Minimum 8 years Business Systems Analysis Role or Equivalent

Demonstrated experience with process analysis, systems analysis, process architectures and systems analysis methodologies and practices including traditional waterfall, Agile, Agile Scrum, UML, UML Enterprise, et cetera.

The Pension Administration BSA 4 applies advanced business process and analysis concepts as a business systems analyst with recognized expertise in pension and benefits. The BSA 4 must apply organizational objectives to resolve highly complex issues in accordance with the UC Retirement System, must have experience in problem-solving complex issues, providing in depth analysis of unique circumstances, and effectively communicating to various audiences and stakeholders. They are able to identify methods, techniques and evaluation criteria to obtain results to support and enhance the UC Retirement System (UCRS) plan administration, business operations, and overall functionality. Please note this is a hybrid position, three days a week on site, located in Oakland, CA.

30% Requirements, Support, and Knowledge Sharing: Analyzes business and user needs and translates them into clear system and process requirements. Provides advanced application support and training, and shares expertise by mentoring other analysts and guiding project work.

25% Process Improvement and Documentation: Initiates and implements improvements to pension administration processes and procedures; prepares and maintains related documentation; and establishes requirements for complex process and system changes.

25% Complex Business and Systems Analysis: Applies advanced knowledge of UCRS plan administration, business processes, and supporting systems to define scope, evaluate impacts, and resolve complex issues in support of current and future operational needs.

20% Systems Design and Testing: Defines system and process requirements and technical specifications for complex changes; develops and coordinates integration and acceptance testing; and may lead cross-functional efforts to resolve significant business or systems issues.
Apply advanced business process and analysis concepts and organizational objectives to resolve highly complex issues.
Business Systems Analyst 4 (TX)
This position is represented by the TX - Technical bargaining unit.
Advanced knowledge of business and process analysis functions.
Advanced knowledge and expertise in pension and benefits.
Advanced knowledge of related areas of IT.
Demonstrated knowledge and expertise in identifying methods, techniques, and evaluation criteria to support and enhance the UC Retirement System.
Knowledge relating to the design of processes and software across the organization.
Advanced skills and methodologies associated with process and software design, modification and implementation.
Demonstrated skills needed to develop process and system implementation plans.
Understanding and skill in complex process and systems requirement documentation standards, such as Use Case modeling, User Story creations and narrative description.
Demonstrated ability to work with others from diverse backgrounds.
Self-motivated and works independently and as part of a team. Able to learn effectively and meet deadlines. Demonstrates problem solving skills.
Advanced knowledge of business processes and procedures.
Demonstrated testing and test planning skills.

Demonstrated effective communication and interpersonal skills. Demonstrated ability to communicate technical information to technical and non-technical personnel at various levels in the organization. Interpersonal and communications skills to work with both technical and non-technical personnel at various levels in the organization.
